source_text: Ista - inquam - quaestio ubi de arbitrio voluntatis et Dei gratia disputatur, ita est ad discernendum, difficilis, ut quando defenditur liberum arbitrium, negari Dei gratia videatur; quando autem asseritur Dei gratia, liberum arbitrium putetur auferri, et cetera
pass_a_gloss: That - inquam - question where about/from by-decision of-will and of-God grace disputatur, so is to discernendum, hard, so-that/as when defenditur free decision, negari of-God grace videatur; when however asseritur of-God grace, free decision let-him-be-thought auferri, and the-rest.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium

pass_b_english: Free will is denied if grace is praised; and, in turn, grace is denied if free will is praised.
When those books themselves begin to be examined, the ungodliness of those statements will be exposed and pierced.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
